If check-ledger-append-sites reports a BYPASS, route the writer through appendReceipt/appendSharded or wrap in withLedgerLock; if check-chained-ledgers reports BROKEN, a tamper-evident chain was altered post-write -- investigate, never silence. # VEILOS

> S113 (2026-06-29) Self-service authority on a handle's OWN protected state is session-proven (1487 tests, SIL 1000). /goal /arc one continuous mission, token-economical by founder direction (a lean self-driven audit, not a 5-agent fan-out). Re-audited S112 vs LIVE FIRST: SOUND (/api/version 6701b9de===HEAD; /api/equity gini 0.1324 with a real top holder; /api/continuum coherence_pillars sum exactly to 935.52; /api/treasury revenue_sources sum to total; /api/persona carries denial_pressure + soul_distance, the dead `denials` field gone). The audit walked the caller-supplied-identity write surface the S112 completeness guard did NOT cover (it matched only the `actorId = ...form.get("actor")` idiom). SECURITY KEYSTONE D-S113.1 (the S112 forgeable-attribution class, one family deeper): two PRIVILEGED self-service lanes still trusted a forgeable form actor — POST /standing/rotate-relay gated on canRelay(<named actor>) (the NAMED handle's Constellar standing, never the requester's, so an unauthenticated POST revoked + re-minted any Constellar's federation relay key = hijack/DoS), and POST /api/portal resolved entitlements[<named actor>].stripe_customer (opening any subscriber's Stripe billing portal — invoices, payment method, cancel). GET /standing also rendered the relay-token bearer secret to anyone who knew the (PUBLIC) handle — fatal because VEILOS publishes handles on /api/equity, /commons, and the leaderboards, so the page's 'handle = bearer credential' premise is false in the wild. FIX: a new session-authoritative resolveSelfServiceActor (sibling to resolveContributionActor) in obelisk/identity.mjs — only a signed session proves ownership (reject auth_required with none; reject not_your_handle on a mismatch; the form actor is NEVER trusted), both lanes route through it, and GET /standing reveals relay-token VALUES + the rotate/billing controls only to the owner's session (viewerActor); a non-owner sees the public 'standing in the open' plan summary. A source-level completeness guard pins the privileged sinks (portal/relay-rotate) can never again be fed a raw form actor — while documenting that payment-INITIATION lanes (/api/checkout, /api/patronage, /api/inscribe, /api/oracle/buy) legitimately pass the payer's claimed actor (the grant is webhook-signature-gated; forging there only GIFTS a victim). No legit owner is stranded: the /return Sovereign-Key flow re-establishes a session. Both carried [SIL] items shipped: #1 (generalize the completeness-guard doctrine to every caller-supplied-identity surface) is realized AS resolveSelfServiceActor + the privileged-sink guard; #2 documented the live-but-undocumented agent claim_secret continuity contract on /agents.json (a continuity block: mint-once, present as `secret`/X-Agent-Secret, required once attested, no recovery + body.secret + updated returns) and a /commons human pointer + a doc-pinning test. +12 tests in tests/s113-self-service-authority.test.mjs; tests/phase29.test.mjs updated to the owner-proven contract. 1475 -> 1487 tests/0, verify 0 (csp 0), worker:check 0, 0 new deps. HONEST DEFER (WIN): the deeper 'should handles be self-authenticating at all' question (passport/standing treat the public handle as a bearer credential) is a founder architectural call — S113 closed the secret/action leaks, not the model. WATCH LIVE next (re-audit S113 vs LIVE first): /api/version === the deployed S113 build; POST /api/portal with no session -> 403 auth_required, with a mismatched session -> 403 not_your_handle; POST /standing/rotate-relay with no session -> 403; GET /standing?id=<a Constellar> as a non-owner shows NO relay-token string; /agents.json participate.continuity documents the claim_secret. LESSON: a completeness guard that matches one idiom (`actorId = form.get`) is blind to the SAME class expressed differently (`canRelay(form.actor)`, `actorId: form.get(...)` in an object literal) — after closing a forgeable-input class, walk the surface the guard CAN'T see and pin the privileged sinks behaviorally; and a 'bearer credential' model is only as safe as the secrecy of the credential — when the same system publishes the handle, the handle cannot authorize anything.
